raw.assessment: The incumbent preserves design selection (40/40) and catches correctable fitting faults before dispatch. Unadjusted small covers take 25–31 minutes, making timely production plausible for that subgroup. Rework concentrates in large covers (5/8 versus 2/14 medium and 0/18 small), but neither cause nor achievable batch median is established. The concrete limiting observation is two customer placement failures on rounded tables absent from the reference set: passing the reference check may not establish customer fit. Estimated waste by weight does not verify the area constraint; observed length shrinkage does not establish width stability or five-cycle durability.

openings.claim: The common cutting allowance may create a repeatable dimensional mismatch on larger covers, causing avoidable rework.
openings.delta: Test a systematic pattern error before propagating it through whole-batch cutting.
openings.prediction: Similar signed dimensional errors recurring on larger covers across operators and designs would support an allowance problem; errors tracking operator or cloth instead would weaken it.
openings.probe: Sew first articles before cutting remaining panels. Record intended, cut, and finished dimensions, design, orientation, operator, and stage times. Repeat any suspected allowance correction before adopting it. Check both axes through the stipulated wash test; calculate revised cutting waste by area and bound expenditure and completion time before scaling.
assumptions: Pilot work can fit within 350 units and three weeks.
Observed size association may be confounded; correction magnitude remains unknown.

openings.claim: Does mismatch in corner geometry explain customer placement failures after accounting for actual tabletop dimensions?
openings.delta: Distinguish inadequate reference geometry from incorrect nominal dimensions.
openings.prediction: Failures among dimensionally matching rounded tables would implicate corner geometry; failures following dimension discrepancies across corner shapes would implicate order measurements.
openings.probe: Ask the six willing customers for actual dimensions and corner outlines. Prioritize the four nominal-only orders where participation overlaps. Record first-placement outcomes against dimension discrepancy and corner shape, including matching square-corner comparisons where available.
assumptions: The willing customers include informative geometry contrasts.
Measurements clarify accepted selections rather than replace them.
Six observations may leave both explanations unresolved.

raw.assessment: Two testable possibilities; neither is established by these observations. Acceptance still requires at least 38 of 40 first placements, every ordered design, median work at most 32 minutes, and all contractual constraints.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: a concealed washable elastic bridge inside each corner pocket could accommodate rounded corners automatically while retaining the ordered visible panels and table-size selection.
openings.delta: Let the hidden anchoring geometry yield locally instead of requiring a rigid pocket to match every corner.
openings.prediction: Compared with fixed pockets on the same panel geometry, bridges improve rounded-table first placements without increasing movement or visible distortion on square tables, including after five wash cycles.
openings.probe: Use retained offcuts for pocket trials. Obtain actual dimensions and corner shapes from the six willing customers. Compare fixed and bridge pockets on rounded customer tables and square reference tables, recording first placement, added sewing time, and wash survival. Adopt only within the 350-unit, three-week envelope, with batch cutting waste measured by area at no more than 8%.
assumptions: Suitable washable elastic is affordable and obtainable.
Corner shape contributes to the observed installation failures.
Added sewing time can fit the batch median target.

openings.claim: Large-cover rework may arise from cumulative seam-feed mismatch or sewing contraction, rather than an incorrect common cutting allowance alone.
openings.delta: Locate when dimensional error appears; if sewing introduces it, test registered seam marks and sewing outward from the midpoint before enlarging panels.
openings.prediction: Sewing-induced error appears between cutting and fitting, grows with seam length, and decreases under the alternate seam sequence. Washing-induced error instead appears principally after washing.
openings.probe: On matched retained strips, compare current and midpoint seam sequences, recording dimensions along both axes before sewing, after sewing, and after five wash cycles. Hold design, cutting direction, and operator constant within pairs. If supported, sew and fit an early large-cover pilot before cutting the remaining batch; record stage times and actual area waste.
assumptions: Retained pieces support useful seam-length comparisons.
Dimensional measurement can distinguish sewing change from cutting error.
A successful strip result transfers to complete covers; the pilot must check this.

openings.claim: Large-cover rework may reflect common allowance error, cumulative sewing contraction/feed mismatch, or washing change.
openings.discriminator: Repeatable signed size error supports allowance; cut-to-sewn change supports sewing; post-wash change supports shrinkage. Operator/design associations may confound size.
openings.probe: Compare current versus marked midpoint-outward seams on matched strips, holding design, orientation and operator constant; measure both axes before/after sewing and five washes. Fit early large-cover articles before batch cutting; repeat suspected allowance correction; record stage times and area waste.
openings.uncertainty: Strip seam lengths, measurement precision, full-cover transfer and correction magnitude remain uncertain.

openings.claim: Customer fit failures may follow corner geometry or actual-versus-nominal dimensions.
openings.discriminator: Failures on dimension-matched rounded tables support geometry; failures tracking dimension discrepancies across shapes support measurement mismatch.
openings.probe: Obtain dimensions and corner outlines from six willing customers, prioritizing nominal-only orders where overlapping; compare first placements with matching square corners where available.
openings.uncertainty: Six customers may lack informative contrasts or leave both causes unresolved.

openings.claim: Concealed washable elastic bridges may let corner pockets accommodate rounded tables.
openings.discriminator: Against fixed pockets with identical panels, improve rounded-table placement without square-table movement or visible distortion, including after washing.
openings.probe: Trial retained offcuts and compare on rounded customer and square reference tables; record placement, sewing time and five-cycle survival.
openings.uncertainty: Geometry causality, elastic availability/cost and added work remain unknown.

lineage.reason: Merged with A2; allowance, sewing and washing distinctions retained.
Merged with Z1; controlled seam-sequence discriminator retained.

post_distill.decision: Probe before adoption. Require at least 38/40 first placements, every ordered size/design, median work <=32 minutes, five-cycle durability and tool-free removal without permanent attachment. Use purchased stock, <=8% waste by area, existing two machines, <=350 units and three weeks. Weight-estimated waste and length-only shrinkage do not establish compliance.
